drafted_from: workflow:keep-the-tools-i-used's own file, tools/workflows/recipes/keep-the-tools-i-used.json (its wake, definition and steps), and the engine's tool-ran fact (trillion-rust src/wake/wake.json ran_fact).
start_here: Say to your AI: "Keep a record of the tools I use." The AI turns on workflow:keep-the-tools-i-used's wake a-tool-ran with your store as its input. From then on, each tool you run is kept in your store once a day, so you can ask which tool you used for something and when.
no_lists_because: It reads nothing: the tool-ran fact carries the tool, whether it answered, the day and the address, and the run keeps one row per tool and state in the person's store (its tools_i_used table).
instructions: 1. Turn on this workflow's wake a-tool-ran with store as the switch's input: where the person keeps the record, its language and the vault name of its login.

2. Run any tool yourself. The person's door tells a tool-ran fact the first time each tool answers (or is refused) each day, for a call of their own, and the run keeps or updates its row in tools_i_used.

3. Read the record in the store: select tool, state, first_day, last_day, days_used, last_address from tools_i_used order by last_day desc. A refused row's last_cause says why the tool did not run; wake:list shows the wake's last firing if a row did not come.

worked_examples.title: A tool the person ran is kept in their store
worked_examples.ask: (the person's door told tool-ran for tool:find-tool-servers-in-a-catalog, answered, on Nov 19 2026)

store.credential_name: the vault name of the person's database login

worked_examples.given: The door told tool-ran {tool tool:find-tool-servers-in-a-catalog, state answered, day_ms of Nov 19 2026}.
worked_examples.hands_back: One row of tools_i_used in the person's store: tool tool:find-tool-servers-in-a-catalog, state answered, first_day and last_day Nov 19 2026, days_used 1; told again on a later day, the same row's last_day moves and days_used becomes 2.
